This is a real CFE-tendered, US-Mexico border gas import pipeline: CFE Director Enrique Ochoa publicly announced it 23 Apr 2014 as the fifth of five new gasoductos (Ehrenberg, Arizona -> San Luis Rio Colorado, Sonora; $250M investment; 130 MMcf/d), reported near-identically by Monitor Economico and Somos Industria (same press event = one origin). It then appears, under its full name 'Ehrenberg - Los Algodones - San Luis Rio Colorado', in SENER/CENACE's PRODESEN 2015-2029 planning document (Tabla 3.1.6 'Gasoductos en Proyecto': CFE-tendered, 160 km, $249M) and again in the PRODESEN 2016-2030 edition (30-May-2016; Tabla 4.1.7: target COD 2017, 160 km, $249M, benefiting Baja California and Sonora), and CENAGAS's Jan-2015 Plan Quinquenal explicitly names it (with Merida-Cancun) as being of a 'caracter comercial' (commercial, not strategic) nature, which is why CENAGAS asked CRE to exclude it from that Plan's evaluation. IEnova/Sempra's own Jul-2014 investor deck lists it as one of 17 market-wide National Infrastructure Program gas-pipeline tender opportunities (160 km, $246M capex, 2014 tender, 1Q2017 COD) -- a private-sector, non-GEM corroboration of existence/specs, distinct from the government sources. CLASSIFICATION as a gas transmission / import-capacity-reinforcement pipeline (not gathering/distribution) is correct: Plan Quinquenal groups it under 'Ductos que refuerzan la capacidad de internacion de gas natural de importacion al norte del pais'. Scope note: all figures found are for the pipeline as a whole (US Ehrenberg, AZ segment -> Mexican San Luis Rio Colorado, Sonora terminus); no source splits a separate US-only vs Mexico-only length/cost/capacity -- GEM's single-segment record for the whole line is the correct scope, not a mismatch.

SCOPE/IDENTITY ESTABLISHED FIRST per the dispatch's scope warning: this is SDG&E's Line 1600, an INTRASTATE natural gas transmission pipeline in San Diego County regulated by the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC), not FERC. Pinned via the worklist Location cells (StartState/Province=California, EndPrefecture/District=San Diego), the wiki page title, and -- decisively -- three independently-sourced, independently-reporting documents (San Diego Union-Tribune x2 by Rob Nikolewski, SDG&E's own News Center via Wayback, and Valley Roadrunner/valleycenter.com x2 by a different reporter) that all describe 'SDG&E's Line 1600' running between Rainbow (near the Riverside/San Diego county line) and Mission Valley/Mission Station, built 1949, serving ~150,000 customers along the I-15 corridor in northern San Diego County -- an exact match to the row's recorded endpoints. EXISTENCE: independently confirmed, real and CPUC-regulated -- not a GEM-only entity. Corroborated further by EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, which tracks a 'Line 1600 Replacement Project' (operator 'San Diego Gas and Electric, SoCalGas', state CA) across 21 releases from March 2020 through Aug 2026, matching this row's Diameter (36 in), Capacity (200 MMcf/d) and SegmentCost ($677,000,000) EXACTLY -- decisive confirmation this EIA-tracked project IS this GEM row (the dispatch brief said the crosswalk found no pre-matched EIA candidate; a manual search of sources/eia_pipeline_projects/data/eia_projects_long.csv by project name found one immediately -- flagging the crosswalk gap). CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified as gas transmission (CPUC/EIA both describe it as a natural gas transmission pipeline replacement/testing project). DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of P2552 (Line 1600's base/system row, swept in slice 1) -- P2553 is specifically the CPUC-approved 'Replacement' capital project (the Pipeline Safety Enhancement Plan hybrid plan, approved Jan 2019/reaffirmed Feb 2020, ~$677M, 19 sub-projects over a 4-year period), a distinct, separately-docketed project on the same physical line -- the same system-row + project-row pattern used elsewhere in this batch (MountainWest, Northern Natural). CAVEAT: an earlier (2018) SDG&E/SoCalGas proposal for a DIFFERENT new parallel line, 'Pipeline 3602' ($639M, would have been 36-inch, would have de-rated Line 1600 instead of replacing it), was rejected by the CPUC in June 2018 (OB Rag, 2018-06-08, https://obrag.org/2018/06/sdges-proposed-pipeline-at-odds-with-san-diegos-climate-action-plan/ -- cited here for context only, not as a proposed_ref for any value, since it describes a different, never-built project). The utilities then returned with the hybrid 'Replacement' plan this row describes. This distinction matters because 'Pipeline 3602' is also 36-inch, which could cause diameter values from the two different projects to be conflated -- see the Diameter fill's notes.

resolutions.recommendation: Correct EndState/Province and EndCountryOrArea to Minnesota / United States; the pipeline as proposed does not physically cross into Canada.
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM records EndState/Province=Manitoba, EndCountryOrArea=Canada, EndPrefecture/District=Emerson-Franklin -- i.e. treats this as a US-Canada border-crossing line. Three independent, dated sources all place the physical terminus in northwestern Minnesota, US, not Canada: (1) WBI Energy's own spokesperson Laura Lueder, quoted on the record in the Pierce County Tribune (2020-02-21): 'Our proposal is to go from the Tioga area to northwestern Minnesota, which is near the Emerson natural gas hub. Our other large gas pipelines connect at that hub and then the gas moves from there to larger markets, such as Chicago.' -- i.e. WBI's own pipe ends in Minnesota near (not at/in) the Emerson hub; (2) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook records State(s)=ND,MN, Beg_State=ND, End_State=MN, and Crosses State Border=Yes (a US interstate designation, not an international one) in every release 2020-03 through 2026-08; (3) offshore-technology.com's project profile states the pipeline 'will start in North Dakota (the US) and ends in Minnesota (the US).' A Federal Register full-text search for '"Tioga to Emerson"' returns zero documents (checked 2026-09-15 via the FederalRegister.gov API), consistent with no DOE/FECM Presidential Permit or FERC Section 3 export/import authorization ever having been sought for this project -- expected if it never crosses the international border. A Canada Energy Regulator site search for the same terms returned no usable results (client-rendered search page, inconclusive either way -- not relied on). The routes-repo geojson's easternmost vertex sits at (-97.208086, 49.005584), about 0.6 km north of the 49th parallel -- fractionally inside Manitoba -- which reads as an artifact of digitizing to the Emerson hub landmark itself rather than evidence the pipe crosses the border; 'Emerson' in the project's own name is the name of the interconnect hub it was designed to reach, not proof its pipe enters Canada. Recommend GEM's end-location cells be corrected to Minnesota/United States (EndPrefecture/District cleared, since 'Emerson-Franklin' is a Manitoba municipality that would no longer apply); no route-geometry replacement is proposed, only the attribute correction. Commodity classification is NOT in question: WBI's own spokesperson calls it 'a large interstate natural gas pipeline system,' EIA classifies it in the Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, and offshore-technology.com calls it 'the onshore gas pipeline' -- this is correctly tracked as gas, not NGL/crude, despite sitting in Bakken oil country.

P2626 is the Trail West/N-MAX project: a proposed ~106-mile, 30-inch interstate gas transmission lateral that would have run from an interconnection with GTN's (Gas Transmission Northwest) system near Madras, Oregon to Northwest Pipeline's (Williams) Grants Pass Lateral near Molalla, Oregon, delivering gas toward the Portland-area market. It was a joint-venture project of Trail West Pipeline, LLC (TWP) / Trail West Holdings (TWH) -- 50% NWN Energy (a NW Natural Holdings subsidiary) and 50% TransCanada American Investments Ltd (a TransCanada/TC Energy subsidiary) -- independently confirmed by two differently-authored, differently-dated sources: Bark, a Mt. Hood-area conservation nonprofit (bark-out.org, page dated 2020-03-10) and Sightline Institute, a Pacific Northwest policy think tank (sightline.org, 2019-06-06 article). Both independently state the same design capacity (500 MMcf/d, doubleable), 30-inch diameter, and 'late 2023' target in-service date, and EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects tracker (28 releases, May 2018 - Aug 2026) independently lists a matching FERC-authority 'Trail West/N-MAX' project (106 miles, $800M, 450 MMcf/d additional capacity, OR-OR, operator of record 'Northwest Pipeline Co'). This is a genuine, distinct sub-project on the Williams Northwest Pipeline system -- NOT a duplicate of any of the other four 'Northwest Gas Pipeline' rows in this batch: P0230 is the aggregate ~3,900-mile NWP system row; P5101 is the Kalama Lateral; P7790 is the Kelso-Beaver Reliability Project; P7812 is the Wild Trail project. No cross_row_leads found this session for those siblings (search-engine access was budget-exhausted and oilandgaswatch.org / S&P Global / Internet Archive were all unreachable this session -- see individual fill notes). Two caveats filed separately below: (1) the sheet's CancelledYear (2023) is not what EIA's release history actually shows -- corrected to 2022 (spec concern); (2) the sheet's Owner (Williams Companies, 100%) is contradicted by both independent sources naming the actual TWP/TWH joint-venture sponsors (attribution concern); (3) EndLocation (Portland) is a market-delivery generalization -- Bark's literal, and the route geojson's, terminus is Molalla, OR (spec concern, corrected in the Location fill directly).

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet's Capacity (3,725 MMcf/d) is stated verbatim in its own cited source (CPUC Summer 2021 Southern California Gas Reliability Assessment, p.2), but that document is explicit that the number is NOT pipeline capacity alone: 'Pipeline and storage capacity combined can provide 3,725 million cubic feet per day (MMcfd) of natural gas' (emphasis added -- executive summary). Confirmed via: (1) Southwest Gas Holdings' own SEC 8-K press release (filed 2026-06-05... actually dated June 2025) announcing the Binding Open Season results for the '2028 Expansion Project'; (2) FERC's Federal Register Notice of Intent to prepare an EA / scoping notice (FR Doc 2026-08459, published 2026-04-30), confirming FERC opened a PRE-FILING docket, No. PF26-5-000, on 2026-01-20, for 'Great Basin's 2028 Expansion Project,' describing planned construction of ~195 mi of new 42-inch pipeline + ~15 mi of new 24-inch lateral pipeline, a new Jungo Road Compressor Station (Humboldt County), a new receipt point adjacent to the existing Opal Valley Receipt Point, and abandonment of ~142 mi of existing 1960s-era 8-/16-inch pipe plus the existing Rye Patch and Lovelock Compressor Stations; (3) Great Basin's own current project microsite (expansion2028.greatbasingtcprojects.com) and its dated August 2026 Fact Sheet PDF, which frames the project as in 'Planning & Development Phase,' anticipated in-service November 2028, with 'Submit FERC application' still a pending 2026 milestone (i.e. no formal NGA section 7 certificate application has been filed as of this sweep -- only the pre-filing docket). CLASSIFICATION confirmed: interstate natural gas transmission pipeline expansion, correctly classified as gas/transmission/proposed. As of this sweep (2026-09-15) no FERC certificate order has issued and no construction has begun -- 'proposed' remains correct (see status_reviews).

resolutions.pipeline_name: Great Basin Gas Transmission Company Pipeline System
resolutions.recommendation: No merge -- keep P7856 (Main Line), P7857 (2024 Expansion), P7858 (Gabbs Lateral NASF Relocation), P7859 (2026 Expansion) and P7860 (2028 Expansion) as five separate rows. Each expansion is a distinct FERC docket/filing for a distinct scope of physical construction on the same underlying system.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Confirmed P7860 is NOT a duplicate/relabeling of any sibling in the 'Great Basin Gas Transmission Company Pipeline System' cluster (P7856-P7860), and specifically not of P7859 despite an EIA data-quality wrinkle (below). Distinguishing facts: P7856 = the 898-mi Main Line itself (operating). P7857 = '2024 Expansion Project,' FERC Docket CP23-466-000, filed 2023-05-01, 3.41 mi (0.25 mi 20-in loop + 2.88 mi 10-in->20-in replacement + 0.28 mi 12-in loop), 5,674 Dth/d incremental capacity. P7858 = 'Gabbs Lateral Naval Air Station Fallon (NASF) Relocation Project,' FERC Docket CP25-551-000 (pre-filing PF24-6-000), filed 2025-09-29. P7859 = '2026 Expansion Project,' FERC Docket CP25-209-000, filed 2025-04-15, 2.32-4.67 mi loop/replacement, 8,129 Dth/d incremental capacity. P7860 (this row) = '2028 Expansion Project,' FERC PRE-FILING Docket PF26-5-000 (opened 2026-01-20; no CP-docket certificate application filed yet as of 2026-08 per the company's own project timeline), a materially larger project spanning six counties, ~195 mi of new 42-in pipe + ~15 mi of new 24-in lateral pipe (~210 mi total new construction) plus abandonment of ~142 mi of old 8-/16-in pipe, targeting ~800 MMcf/d (per EIA's most current releases, based on binding precedent agreements) to as much as 948,000 Dth/d (per the company's own August 2026 Fact Sheet) of incremental capacity, in-service targeted November 2028, capital cost ~$1.7B (EIA) vs. an earlier June-2025 Southwest Gas estimate of $800M-$1.2B. EIA DATA-QUALITY NOTE (relevant to the misattribution precedent the orchestrator flagged): EIA's own 'Great Basin Expansion Project' row (Natural Gas Pipeline Projects sheet, present in the 2026-01/05/08 releases) is confirmed to be THIS row (P7860, the 2028 Expansion) by its own Notes text -- 'Larger 2028 Expansion in pre-filing discussions with FERC,' explicitly distinguished in the same Notes from 'a smaller 2026 Expansion (~8,129 Dth/d)... filed FERC CP25-209-000 on 4/15/2025' (i.e. P7859) -- but the Aug-2026 release's 'Docket/Permit Number' FIELD (as opposed to the Notes prose) is populated with 'CP25-209-000,' which is actually P7859's docket, not P7860's. This is an EIA data-entry error in that one structured field, not evidence the two rows are the same project -- the correct docket citation for P7860 is FERC PF26-5-000 / Federal Register FR Doc 2026-08459, never any EIA-stated 'CP25-209-000.' Routed as informational here; no cross_row_lead needed since P7859's own shard already resolved this correctly.

resolutions.pipeline_name: Great Basin Gas Transmission Company Pipeline System
resolutions.recommendation: Correct LengthKnown from 0.00 to ~210 mi (195 mi new 42-in mainline loop + 15 mi new 24-in lateral, per FERC's own scoping notice) and Diameter from blank to 42,24 in. The sheet's 0.00/blank pairing is currently cited to the pgjonline.com article, but that article never states a segment mileage at all -- it only mentions Great Basin's existing 898-mile SYSTEM total, which is a different scope (aggregate-vs-segment rule) -- so the Length cell was effectively uncited despite carrying a [ref]. Two independent, current, primary sources (FERC's own regulatory scoping notice and Great Basin's own August-2026 Fact Sheet) agree the 2028 Expansion Project involves substantial NEW physical pipe, not zero -- but they disagree on the exact total: FERC's itemized figure sums to 210 mi (195+15); the company's own Fact Sheet instead states 'approximately 230 miles of natural gas pipeline and associated facilities' (no diameter breakdown given). That is a genuine, unreconciled ~9.5% delta between two credible primary sources (regulator vs. applicant), not simple rounding -- recommend using FERC's itemized 195+15=210 mi / 42,24-in figures (more granular, matches the Diameter field's need for a breakdown) as the staged fill, with the company's differing 230-mi aggregate flagged here for reconciliation once a formal certificate application (with a final engineering route sheet) is filed.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Checked the pgjonline.com article word-for-word: it states only 'the company's 898-mile transmission system' (the Main Line total, P7856's scope) and gives no segment-specific mileage or diameter for the 2028 Expansion -- confirms the current [ref] does not actually support LengthKnown=0.00/Diameter=blank. FERC's Notice of Intent To Prepare an Environmental Assessment / scoping notice (FR Doc 2026-08459, published 2026-04-30, Docket PF26-5-000): 'The 2028 Expansion Project would consist of approximately 195 miles of new 42-inch-diameter pipeline and approximately 15 miles of new 24-inch-diameter lateral pipelines... [and] the planned abandonment of approximately 142 miles of existing, mostly 1960s-era, 8- and 16-inch-diameter pipeline and the existing Rye Patch and Lovelock Compressor Stations.' Great Basin's own August 2026 Fact Sheet (expansion2028.greatbasingtcprojects.com): 'Installation of approximately 230 miles of natural gas pipeline and associated facilities, one new compressor station, and modifications to existing infrastructure' -- confirms substantial new construction and the abandonment total (~142 mi, matching FERC) but gives a higher aggregate new-mileage figure with no diameter split. Both sources independently rule out 0.00/blank as correct; staged the FERC figure as the primary fill (see fills[]) and filed this as a spec concern rather than silently picking one number, since a formal certificate application (which would carry the definitive engineering figure) has not yet been filed.

resolutions.pipeline_name: Great Basin Gas Transmission Company Pipeline System
resolutions.recommendation: Capacity=1250.00 MMcf/d is sourced (the cited pgjonline.com article does state 'approximately 1.25 billion cubic feet per day,' via unit equivalence 1.25 Bcf/d = 1250 MMcf/d -- kept as REVERIFIED, see fills[]) but it is Southwest Gas's own June-2025 PRE-close estimate, based on 'indicative capacity requests' before the Binding Open Season and its two supplemental rounds had even closed. Two later, more current sources give materially different figures and disagree with EACH OTHER: EIA's own May/Aug-2026 releases state 'nearly 800 MMcf/d of binding precedent agreements' actually secured across three completed open seasons (closing 5/28/2025, 11/11/2025, and December 2025) -- EIA's Jan-2026 release had shown 1,760 MMcf/d, since revised down; while Great Basin's own August-2026 Fact Sheet instead states the project 'adds up to approximately 948,000 dekatherms per day' (~948 MMcf/d, roughly Dth/Mcf-equivalent) of new capacity -- a THIRD figure, using 'up to,' suggesting a maximum/design capacity rather than the contracted 800 MMcf/d EIA reports. Recommend investigating and updating once the formal FERC application publishes a definitive contracted capacity figure; in the meantime EIA's 800 MMcf/d (grounded in EIA's own description of actual signed binding precedent agreements, the most concrete and recent commercial fact available) is the better-evidenced replacement candidate over the stale 1250, but the company's own newer 948,000 Dth/d figure is a live, unreconciled alternative -- not confident enough in either single number to overwrite Capacity outright, so left the candidate value blank here pending that reconciliation.
resolutions.researcher_notes: pgj/SEC (June 2025, 8-K press release, single origin): 'Approximately 1.25 billion cubic feet per day of incremental transportation capacity' -- an ESTIMATE based on indicative (non-binding) capacity requests, explicitly framed as subject to change pending final negotiated precedent agreements. EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, 'Great Basin Expansion Project' row: Jan-2026 release = 1,760 MMcf/d; May-2026 and Aug-2026 releases both = 800 MMcf/d, with EIA's own Notes text explaining the drop: 'Binding open season closed 5/28/2025, followed by supplemental open seasons (one closing 11/11/2025, a second closing December 2025) that together secured nearly 800 MMcf/d of binding precedent agreements (20-year minimum term)' -- i.e. EIA's revision reflects the ACTUAL contracted outcome of the open season process the pgj estimate predated. Great Basin's own August-2026 Fact Sheet: 'Adds up to approximately 948,000 dekatherms per day of new natural gas transportation capacity' -- current as of the same month as this sweep, from the applicant itself, but does not reconcile with EIA's 800 MMcf/d figure and uses 'up to' phrasing. All three figures trace to genuinely different vintages/definitions (indicative estimate vs. contracted binding capacity vs. a design/maximum figure), not a simple correction chain -- filed as a material, unresolved spec concern per rule 5 rather than silently staging any one of them as a correction.

This row is a PROJECT, not the REX system: the 'Critical Energy Reliability Link' (CERL), a proposed REX expansion (FERC Docket CP25-539-000, applicants Rockies Express Pipeline LLC / Cheyenne Connector, LLC / East Cheyenne Gas Storage, LLC) to serve Colorado Springs Utilities, filed 2025-08-15. Existence confirmed independently: the Federal Register notice of application (federalregister.gov, 90 FR 42758, 2025-09-04) states the same scope, and the operator's own project site (criticalenergyreliabilitylink.com) and EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (Aug 2026 release, row 31, docket CP25-539-000) both corroborate it as an active, real application. No duplicate: none of the other 41 rows in this batch's roster is REX or CERL, and REX's other rows (mainline, Entrega phases, REX-East) are swept in slice 1 / other batches, not this roster -- no double-count risk found. Classification correct: NGA section 7(b)/7(c) interstate certificate application = transmission-jurisdictional (PipelineType=transmission), commodity natural gas (Fuel=Gas). Caveats, each filed as its own record below: StartYear1 is wrong (sheet 2027, sourced true in-service year is 2028 -- see the spec concern below); ConstructionYear, SegmentCost, Diameter and Owner1/2/3-only-Operator support in this shard rest on a single verified origin each (the FERC docket / operator's own site), so they are staged at medium tier pending a second independent source. Of the 30 wiki-harvested citations for this gem.wiki page, only 2 (oilandgaswatch.org and criticalenergyreliabilitylink.com) concern THIS 2025 project; the other 28 are about the historical 2005-2020 REX mainline (original construction, Entrega phases I/II, Kinder Morgan/Sempra/ConocoPhillips/Tallgrass ownership transactions) and do not apply to this segment -- checked their titles/dates/context against the CERL scope and none names or states a value for the Critical Energy Reliability Link Project. Orchestrator note: proposed_refs were empty on this record while it claimed tier=high / independent=true. A validity record carries no verifications by convention, so its tier is counted over proposed_refs -- an empty list reads as zero publishers and contradicts the claimed tier. The three sources the prose already names as independently confirming existence (federalregister.gov 90 FR 42758; criticalenergyreliabilitylink.com, the operator's own project site; eia.gov Aug-2026 release, row 31) are now listed, which is what the high/independent claim actually rests on: three distinct publishers.
